language_wrapper: Consider a regular {n_sides}-prism. On each of its {n_sides} lateral rectangular faces, draw both face diagonals so that each face has one intersection point at its center. Now, apply two structural choices: (i) lateral edges are included according to [include_vertical_edges] (True = kept, False = removed), and (ii) the intersection points are connected into a cycle around the prism according to [connect_centers] (True = connected, False = not connected). We then perform a {num_colors}-coloring of all 2·{n_sides} original prism vertices together with the {n_sides} intersection points, subject to the rule that adjacent vertices in this constructed graph must receive distinct colors. Two colorings that coincide after any rotation around the central axis are regarded as the same. Determine the number of such inequivalent colorings.
hardness_rationale: The family extends the seed prism-coloring problem by simultaneously parameterizing the number of sides n, the number of colors k, and two structural toggles: whether vertical lateral edges are kept and whether the intersection points are connected into a cycle. Even when only rotations are factored out, counting fixed colorings requires a weighted transfer-matrix approach on a state space of size roughly k^3 (reducing to k(k−1)·k when vertical edges are kept). The adjacency constraints now involve cross-face interactions through center vertices and, optionally, center-to-center constraints, necessitating matrix exponentiation and Burnside averaging over divisors of n. This is strictly more complex than the original, which has fixed parameters and fewer adjacency relations, and is not amenable to simple guessing; it requires advanced combinatorial enumeration and linear-algebraic techniques (cycle index via traces of matrix powers).
notes: Implementation uses a transfer-matrix M indexed by states (t_i, b_i, c_i), encoding top, bottom, and center colors at face i. Transitions enforce cycle adjacency (top/bottom inequality), cross-face center constraints, and optional center cycle inequality. Burnside’s lemma over rotations yields the final count via sum of traces of M^d for d dividing n weighted by Euler’s totient. Parameter ranges are chosen to keep verification tractable while maintaining non-triviality.
source_question: Consider a regular 25-prism. By connecting the face diagonals of each lateral face, 25 intersection points are generated, and then the lateral edges are removed. Now, we perform a three-coloring on these 25 intersection points and 50 vertices, where adjacent vertices cannot have the same color. Colorings that coincide after rotation around the central axis are regarded as the same kind. Find the number of coloring methods.
